body:
The golden path for "I want this `.md` to render when I visit it in Chrome":

```
1. User navigates to file:///path/to/foo.md
2. Chrome loads the page with default text/plain handling
3. Our content script (handler.ts) runs at document_end
   - url matches /\.(md|mdx|markdown|json|jsonc)(\?.*)?(#.*)?$/i
   - settings.formats[ext] enabled? (reads chrome.storage.sync)
   - sessionStorage["fv-handled"] === url? → bail (re-entry guard)
4. fetch(url) → raw file text
   - (fallback: document.querySelector("pre")?.textContent)
5. chrome.storage.session.set({ [key]: { url, content, name } })
6. location.replace(chrome-extension://…/src/app/index.html?intercept=<key>)
7. Viewer tab loads; App.tsx pickupIntercept() reads the key
8. intercept.ts builds LibraryFile { id: "intercept:<url>", sourceUrl, content }
9. addFiles + setActive → the file appears in the library + tab strip
10. urlSync rewrites ?intercept=<key> → ?file=<id> (shareable)
```

**Requires** the user to have enabled "Allow access to file URLs" on the
extension details page — Chrome gates that behind an explicit toggle per
extension.
